Auto Parts Brands — OEM & Aftermarket Part Numbers

Catalog updated · Sep 2026·504 Brands·20,858,993 Part numbers·Find a vehicle

Every part in this catalog carries its brand and manufacturer part number — that is what makes cross-referencing possible. Browse all 504 brands below (20,858,993 part numbers total), from OE suppliers like Motorcraft, ACDelco and Mopar to aftermarket makers such as Dorman, Bosch and Power Stop.

Open a brand to see its numbers; each listing links to the years, models and engines it is confirmed to fit. If you already know the stamped number on an old part, search it from the finder or jump into the brand page and filter by number.

Need parts for a specific vehicle instead of a brand? Use Find a vehicle below to cascade make → year → model → engine, then land on the category that matches the job.

OE Suppliers, Aftermarket Manufacturers, and What the Difference Means

A large share of the "aftermarket" brands in this catalog are the same companies that supply parts to vehicle assembly lines — they simply box the identical part under their own name once the vehicle ships. Others are pure aftermarket manufacturers building to the original specification, often at a lower price and sometimes with improvements the factory part never got. Both publish formal application data, and that data — not the label on the box — is what this catalog is built on.

Every one of the 20,858,993 parts across these 504 brands carries its manufacturer part number and verified vehicle fitment down to the engine. That means you can start from a brand you trust and drill into its catalog, or start from a part number on an old part and let the search tell you which brand made it and what it fits. Either direction ends at the same place: a fitment-verified part you can cross-reference before ordering.

Frequently Asked Questions

What brands are included in this catalog?

504 parts manufacturers with 20,858,993 parts between them — original-equipment suppliers, established aftermarket names and specialty manufacturers. Each brand page lists its parts with part numbers and the vehicles they're verified to fit.

Are OE-supplier parts better than aftermarket parts?

Not automatically. Many OE suppliers sell the exact assembly-line part under their own box, while quality aftermarket brands build to the same specification at a lower price. What matters is verified fitment and the right grade for how the vehicle is used — both of which are visible on every part here.

How do I look up a part if I know the brand and part number?

Open the brand's page and search the number, or put the part number straight into the site search. The result shows the part and every year, model and engine it has published fitment for — which doubles as a cross-reference check against your vehicle.

Can I cross-reference a discontinued part number to a current brand?

Usually, yes. Search the old number to find its fitment record, then open the same subcategory for your vehicle — the other brands listed there cover the same application. That subcategory view is effectively a live cross-reference table for that part.
